text: This framework is particularly relevant for interpreting qualitative accounts of CSAM users that emphasize internal conflict, fluctuating control, and context-dependent behavior rather than stable offending trajectories. In relation to CSAM offending, Seto argues that individuals who use child sexual abuse material may have pedophilic or hebephilic sexual interests, but often show lower antisociality, higher self-control or fewer facilitating factors, greater access to Internet technologies, and less access to children than individuals who committ contact sexual offenses against children ( 62 , 68 ).
source_label: Identity under threat: internal conflict and stigma in undetected child sexual abuse material users
